See AMC.939 (c)
(a) Turbine engine powerplant operating characteristics must be investigated in flight to determine that no adverse characteristics (such as stall, surge, or flameout) are present, to a hazardous degree, during normal and emergency operations within the range of operating limitations of the UAV and of the engine.
(b) Turbocharged reciprocating engine operating characteristics must be investigated in flight to an appropriate degree to assure that no adverse characteristics, such as a result of an inadvertent overboost, surge, flooding, or vapour lock, are present during normal or emergency operation of the engine(s) throughout the range of operating limitations of both UAV and engine.
(c) For turbine engines, the air inlet system must not, as a result of airflow distortion during normal operation, cause vibration harmful to the engine or instability greater than that allowed by the engine specification.
